subject.title: [Bug]: Slack `allowBots: true` silently drops all bot messages unless `allowFrom` contains an explicit owner user ID

question: Should Slack add an explicit opt-in all-bot room admission mode, or keep the owner-presence guard and only warn on wildcard-only or ownerless `allowBots` configs?
rationale: The source path is clear, but changing wildcard or all-bot admission would alter the Slack bot-relay security boundary created for the prior owner-presence fix.

options.title: Warn and preserve guard
options.body: Add Slack config, doctor, or startup diagnostics for inert wildcard-only `allowBots` room setups while keeping explicit owner presence or per-channel bot allowlists required by default.

options.title: Add explicit all-bot mode
options.body: Accept a clearly named opt-in mode that bypasses owner presence for bot-authored room messages, with security docs and regression tests for guarded and unguarded behavior.

options.title: Treat wildcard as owner presence
options.body: Make wildcard `allowFrom` satisfy the room bot gate, restoring intuitive wildcard behavior but weakening the previous owner-presence security boundary for existing configs.

recommendation.title: Warn and preserve guard
recommendation.body: Add Slack config, doctor, or startup diagnostics for inert wildcard-only `allowBots` room setups while keeping explicit owner presence or per-channel bot allowlists required by default.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the owner-presence guard and are the clearest routed owner for deciding whether to preserve or relax that Slack security boundary.
